reaction.episode: The current episode is DIGESTION, not capitulation: SPX closed October 23 at 7,623.68, down 2.82% from its 120-day high, 0.99% below its 50-day and 4.56% above its 200-day, with SMH between zones at $527.20 (down 21.53% from its high) and NVDA just above Zone 1 at $210.96, VIX at 19.45, HY OAS calm at 3.23, and only 1 of 4 mechanical capitulation signals confirmed. Episode data is fresh through October 23, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: A held close above SPX $7,750–7,820 with SMH above $600 and VIX rolling over proves Watch too cautious and voids the ladder; conversely HY OAS above 4% with SPX below its 200-day proves the digestion read wrong in the other direction and replaces this ladder with a regime-break response.

ladder.response: Stand down from probing: the digestion read is broken, freeze new entries and re-underwrite the book for a regime break rather than a rotation

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail pattern is the live risk: SPX already closed back below the $7,750–7,820 failure zone, so any bounce into that zone that fails again is the bull trap. Entries must not chase the first bounce — wait for the failure-zone retest verdict (a held close above, or a confirmed failure) and require zone prints plus a rising capitulation tally before probing.

strategyPosture: Watch, with a shopping list ready: the broad market is digesting, not breaking, while AI hardware and select power names offer DATA_AHEAD dislocations — but with only 1 of 4 mechanical capitulation signals confirmed, entries stay staged at zones, not chased on bounces.

themes.counterRead: Weakness is concentrated in the names that dominated the index, not spread across the market: the strongest Mag7 name, AAPL, is only 1.1% below its high while the weakest, TSLA, is 25.4% below. Treating leadership unwind as a broad-market break risks selling an index that is still holding above its 200-day into a rotation. The divergence itself is the signal to track, since credit conditions can flip — but today they have not.
themes.dataAnchor: The broad index does not confirm a rollover. SPX closed October 23 at 7,623.68, only 2.82% below its 120-day high of 7,844.52 and still 4.56% above its 200-day average of 7,291.31, while SPY is just 2.8% below its 52-week high. The Mag7 average sits 13.99% below 52-week highs against SPY's 2.8% — an 11.19-point divergence gap — and bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). The input's own readState is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER.
themes.label: Leadership rotation, not a broad rollover
themes.narrative: The tape feels like a broad meltdown: the month's laggard board is a wall of red, with SMR down 37.19%, ASTS down 35.34%, CONL down 34.28%, OKLO down 31.26% and RKLB down 28.70% over one month, and the AI-power complex leading the decline.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS moving off 0% toward stress, or the SPY-to-52-week-high gap widening past 5% alongside HY OAS above 4%.

themes.counterRead: This is the classic DATA_AHEAD setup the screen is built to catch: price and fundamentals moving in opposite directions. But multiple compression is real in this group — AMAT's own decline reason is MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION — so the opportunity is in staged, zone-based entries, not in calling the bottom on a single print. NVDA, the conviction promotion at score 83, is only 13.3% off its high versus 35-49% for the equipment names, so it is the least dislocated of the set.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data runs the other way. AVGO revenue is growing 55% year over year with a 67.8% gross margin and $26,914M of free cash flow while the stock sits 35.0% below its high; NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% while 13.3% below its peak; LRCX revenue is up 131.3% at 47.5% below its high; CLS revenue is up 57.8% at 45.1% below; ONTO revenue is up 22.1% at 48.6% below; AMAT revenue is up 11.4% at 49.0% below. RSI readings across the group (AVGO 34.2, ONTO 26.5, LRCX 24.6, CLS 28.2, AMAT 26.1) mark washed-out positioning, not broken businesses — except MU, flagged ACUTE_CATALYST at 30.1% below its high and down 18.8% over one month, which is the exception to verify separately.
themes.label: AI hardware: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market narrative is that the AI hardware trade is broken: SMH is down 21.53% from its 120-day high and 13.08% over 20 days, and the semiconductor dislocation list runs deep, with AMAT 49.0% below its high, LRCX 47.5%, CLS 45.1% and ONTO 48.6%.
themes.watchFor: SMH printing into Zone 2 ($470–505) or reclaiming its 50-day ($575.09); NVDA holding or losing Zone 1 ($200–210).

themes.counterRead: Do not buy the theme; buy the verified names inside it. BWXT's growth-plus-dislocation profile is the DATA_AHEAD pocket within a NARRATIVE_AHEAD theme, while VST's deteriorating revenue means its insider buying is a watch item, not a buy signal. The theme's next leg depends on whether the unwind stabilizes into stock-picking or keeps compressing the whole complex together.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals split the group rather than vindicating it wholesale. BWXT revenue is growing 26.1% year over year while the stock sits 47.4% below its high — a genuine dislocation inside the theme — but VST, the watchlist promotion at score 78, carries DETERIORATING revenue inflection even with $1.17M of insider buying at its trough price of $140.16, 31.2% below its high. VST's own trend is only +1.6% over one month against PWR's -15.1% and GEV's -14.87%, so the power complex is not moving as one trade.
themes.label: Nuclear, power and space: the story ran past the data
themes.narrative: Nuclear, power-infrastructure and space names were priced as if the buildout were already banked, and the unwind is violent: over one month GEV is down 14.87%, PWR down 15.31%, URA down 16.37%, OKLO down 31.26% and SMR down 37.19%, while RKLB is down 28.70% and ASTS down 35.34%.
themes.watchFor: BWXT holding its dislocation without a revenue guide-down; VST revenue inflection turning from DETERIORATING, or its $140.16 trough failing.

themes.counterRead: Rates near 5% explain the multiple compression in AI hardware without requiring a credit event, and credit calm explains why the index holds above its 200-day while leadership unwinds. The alignment breaks if either leg moves: a 10-year sustainably above 5% with HY OAS widening would turn a digestion into a regime break; a dovish FOMC surprise against this positioning would instead release the compressed multiples.
themes.dataAnchor: The rate and credit data match that nervous-but-orderly tape. The 10-year sits at 4.99% with the 2-year at 4.77% and the 2s10s curve at +0.22; the real 10-year is 2.64% and breakeven inflation (T10IE) is 2.35%. Credit is not cracking: HY OAS is 3.23, the one confirmed signal in the mechanical tally, and the episode block marks credit calm. VIX is 19.45, up 30.8% over 20 days and at its 5-day high, but with no spike rollover — elevated, not panicked. The Fed funds effective rate is 3.88%.
themes.label: Rates near 5%, credit calm, FOMC as the gate
themes.narrative: Ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC decision, the market is pricing a rates-and-inflation test: the September CPI print is still an active event signal and headlines cite elevated oil prices stoking inflation fears into next week's Fed meeting.
themes.watchFor: 10-year sustained above 5.00% or HY OAS above 4%; the October 27–28 FOMC outcome versus the 4.99% 10-year starting point.
